ACT Certification | CRM proposal

Proposed build for ACT Certification · Draft for discussion

Executive summary

We propose a custom CRM for ACT Certification that connects an enquiry to its proposal, signed documents, payment and assessment. The purpose is to reduce repeated data entry and manual status checks, and give the team one clear record of each job, its documents, owner and next action.

The problems and their impact

ACT’s walkthrough described requests arriving through Jotform, followed by staff re-entering the details into BCS. Staff then prepare proposals and forms, and check signing and payment separately before progressing the job.

Repeated entry and document preparation. The same request details are handled twice, then used to assemble proposals and forms. This takes staff away from progressing jobs and creates more opportunities for errors.

Separate signing, payment and job status. Staff must check different systems to know what can move forward. A signed proposal or paid invoice can still need a manual handoff.

Documents, ownership and workload. The team needs clearer approved and superseded document versions, assigned tasks and workload visibility. Without these, people spend time checking files and asking who is doing what next.

Cost of the current process: ACT’s job volume, handling time and staff cost still need to be measured before a dollar saving can be agreed.

Proposed solution

Build separate enquiry, proposal and project views around one connected job record. Bring Jotform requests into the CRM; prepare proposals from approved templates; show DocuSign and Xero status; and assign the next task when a job is ready. Keep Microsoft’s inspection calendar, with booking confirmations and reminders. Organise plans by version and status. Staff still approve fees, proposals and all certification decisions.

Timeline

  1. Confirm scope: Map the workflow, agree the first release and confirm system access.
  2. Build and connect: Create the CRM, document templates and agreed integrations.
  3. Test with the team: Run sample jobs through the full process and resolve issues.
  4. Launch and train: Train staff, agree the cutover and provide launch support.

Dates will be agreed after scope and integration access are confirmed.
